name: this Mutation
essence: When a method mutates this, every caller is coupled to call order.

examples.summary: `Record` has a value receiver, so `c.hits++` mutates a copy.
examples.mechanism: Value receivers get a copy of the struct; writes do not reach the caller.

examples.summary: Method value `t.Report` copies `t` at binding time, so it reports the stale target.
examples.mechanism: Method values with value receivers evaluate and copy the receiver when created.

examples.summary: Assigning the struct to an interface stores a copy; raising the limit afterwards has no effect on the policy.
examples.mechanism: Interface values box a copy of non-pointer values.

examples.summary: `peek(&self)` advances the cursor through `Cell`, so two peeks return different tokens.
examples.mechanism: Interior mutability lets a `&self` method mutate state, hiding call-order coupling from the signature.

examples.summary: Passing `tracker.handle` detaches it from its receiver; `this` is undefined when invoked.
examples.mechanism: Method references don't carry `this`; class bodies are strict mode.
examples.observed_output:
error: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'clicks')
clicks: 0

examples.summary: Methods mutate `this.subtotal` in place, so totals depend on call order and retries compound tax.
examples.mechanism: Each call reads state written by previous calls instead of deriving from inputs.
examples.observed_output:
tax then coupon: 100
coupon then tax: 99
tax retried: 121
examples.expected_behavior: consistent total regardless of order; idempotent tax

examples.summary: Builder mutates and returns `this`; two queries branched from one base share every filter.
examples.mechanism: Fluent API returns the same mutable instance rather than a new builder.
examples.observed_output:
SELECT * FROM users WHERE active = true AND role = 'admin' AND role = 'guest'
SELECT * FROM users WHERE active = true AND role = 'admin' AND role = 'guest'
examples.expected_behavior: admins: active AND admin / guests: active AND guest

examples.summary: Arrow-function class field is assigned on the instance, shadowing the subclass's prototype override.
examples.mechanism: Instance fields are set in the base constructor and take precedence over prototype methods.

examples.summary: `function` callback passed to setTimeout gets Node's Timeout object as `this`; the session flag is written onto the timer.
examples.mechanism: Non-arrow functions rebind `this` to the caller-chosen receiver.

examples.summary: Ben's post changes Ada's balance, because both ledgers share one lines list.
examples.mechanism: self.lines looks up the class list when the instance has no lines of its own, and append mutates that list.

examples.summary: Staff.seed reads bonus during Account.__init__, before that attribute exists.
examples.mechanism: The base initializer calls an overridable method, and the override runs before the subclass body.

examples.summary: render calls banner with no instance, so the owner never gets through.
examples.mechanism: Assigning a function onto an instance does not bind self. The call passes only the arguments in parentheses.
examples.observed_output: TypeError: banner() missing 1 required positional argument: 'self'

examples.summary: with_sku changes the order and then returns None, so the next attribute read fails.
examples.mechanism: A method returns None unless it returns self. The chained call therefore has no sku.
